newsitem.title: UK: Biotech files 1st drug marketing application.
newsitem.headline: Biotech files 1st drug marketing application.

text.p: British biotechnology company British Biotech Plc said on Wednesday it had made its first Marketing Authorisation Application to the European Medicines Evaluation Agency for its Zacutex pancreatitis treatment.

"Submitting the European Marketing Authorisation Application on target marks a landmark in the history of the company since this is the first British Biotech drug to have completed clinical trials and be pending registration," Biotech's chief executive Keith McCullagh said in a statement.
The Oxford-based research group's clinical trials of the drug Lexipafant, to be sold under the name Zacutex, showed it helped to combat liver and kidney failure induced by acute pancreatitis.

There is currently little on the market to treat the condition, which kills up to 10 percent of all sufferers. Some 100,000 people in western Europe and 200,000 in the U.S. suffer from acute pancreatitis each year.
Analysts have predicted sales of up to $300 million for Zacutex. British Biotech said last year it did not expect regulators to block the drug.
McCullagh said manufacturing and pre-marketing activities were under way in Europe and the group was continuing clinical development of both Zacutex and marimastat, its anti-cancer pill.
Biotech said the marimastat development programme continued to expand, with 20 Phase II and four Phase III clinical trials completed or under way.
